Luce, Boston, 1906) both read Eternity is in love with the productions of time., standing alone. It is the tenth Proverb of Hell, between He whose face gives no light, shall never become a star. and The busy bee has no time for sorrow. That matches the Erdman reading the verifier cites. The Proverbs of Hell begin on plate 7 and the tenth falls well inside that plate's first run, so plate 7 holds. A May refuter established the same for the first proverb against the plate-derived transcriptions. Attribution: Blake's own engraved aphorism, no trap on the misattribution list. It is authored, so not an anonymous proverb and not out of scope. shipped.js: not shipped, no near line, Blake at 0 of 3, not banned. The source line leads with the name, has no dash and runs 80 characters. 1790 is the conventional date, on plate 3, though the book was etched over 1790 to 1793. Poetry is the tag used for the Marriage in May, and it is defensible for an illuminated prophetic book. It is publishable and on theme: time's works loved by what does not die. The weakest point is that the verifier opened no page, but I did, and the text agrees.
